soundness_flags.label: prop:two-arm-regression-check
soundness_flags.one_line: It depends on thm:qstar-second-order, whose declared assumptions require |S_c|≥3, while this proposition changes to |S_c|=2; the stated dependency cannot supply the claimed regression.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorems 2.1–2.3 and 3.1; HTML lines 93–134 and Appendix C lines 432–440
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces the binary two-arm experiment to a scalar binomial problem and proves rho_n*=n^-1-C_A n^-4/3+o(n^-4/3), attained by Bernoulli(1/2) assignment and nonlinear shrinkage.
For bounded two-arm potential outcomes, the unrestricted-design and measurable-estimator minimax value is attained by iid Bernoulli(0.5) assignment with a nonlinear estimator.

The paper studies finite-sample minimax randomization under permutation-invariant distribution classes and characterizes complete randomization with linear estimator schemes under additional assumptions.
The paper gives first-order asymptotic efficiency bounds for sequential, covariate-adaptive experimental designs and states extensions to multiple treatments with constraints.

Within design-unbiased estimation of bounded finite-population totals, pairwise-independent inclusion is the exact condition for the sharp fixed-design bound, and independent sampling attains the joint design-and-estimator optimum.
The paper develops limit-of-experiments asymptotic optimality theory for statistical treatment rules in smooth parametric and semiparametric models under average and minimax criteria.
